rationale: B wins because it found the sharper extra protagonist A left on the table: “Sephora is betting more shelf on a brand whose numbers nobody outside can see.” A’s “A brand born from a beauty blog is now betting on the perfume aisle” is a softer product-launch wrapper that needs fragrance facts the update does not provide. Both sets are usable; B is just more likely to stop the founder before they pitch the easy-but-thin version.
gaps_in_A: “A brand born from a beauty blog is now betting on the perfume aisle” treats the fragrance launch as a viable angle without product names, price, notes, perfumer, or category context. That is a product listing wearing a feature hat.
“collapse of the direct-to-consumer thesis” overstates what one Glossier channel claim can prove. The set flags the proof gap, but the headline frame still swings bigger than the supplied facts.
A misses the clean retailer-protagonist angle: what Sephora’s expanded allocation says when Glossier itself discloses no revenue or profitability.
gaps_in_B: “suburban strip-mall retail rather than mall-and-city Sephora” is colorful, but the update only says Sephora at Kohl’s. That retail geography is inferred, not supplied.
“Sephora and LVMH’s specialty-retail strategy” brings in LVMH, which is not in the update. True in the real world is not the same as grounded in the provided brief.
“one of the few brands with a clean twelve-year arc” is an unsupported comparative claim. The update gives the dates; it does not give the peer set.
